newsitem.title: GERMANY: Floods hit German towns, Rhine tributaries closed.
newsitem.headline: Floods hit German towns, Rhine tributaries closed.

text.p: German authorities suspended shipping on three major Rhine tributaries on Wednesday as heavy rainfall swelled rivers in the southwest of the country and threatened to flood several towns.
In Saarbruecken near the French border, banks asked customers to empty safe deposit boxes in underground vaults as the Saar river burst its banks and began to encroach on the town centre.

Flood barriers were erected to protect Heidelberg as the Neckar river looked like spilling over the town's embankment, but authorities said they did not think the university town's historic centre, which lies higher, would be flooded.
Apart from the Neckar and Saar, the Moselle was also closed to shipping as the river rose four metres in the space of 24 hours in some places, including the city of Trier.
Despite the sudden rise in the Rhine's tributaries, river authorities in Mainz said shipping traffic on Germany's main waterway was continuing as normal.
They said most of the rivers would have reached their peak levels by Thursday, and that there was little chance that Rhine traffic would have to be suspended.
